design: Tool-free battery swap on the battery-on-cap backpack (D-037, qilinxiaoxiang/microduck_rl 8bce48af): a 32 x 12.6 mm opening in the roof straight above the battery (frame and cap, across the cap seam; the cradle roof tab goes), and a printed hatch over it. The hatch has two fixed front tabs under the frame roof edge, a side snap tongue at the rear left whose hook catches under the cap roof edge, a grip tab behind the box to push the tongue in and lift the hatch, a rib that holds the battery down 0.3 mm above its top, and lead notches open to the rear edge. The two retainer bars stay screwed and are no longer removed; the switch, DFR1202, box outline and fixing are unchanged. The battery lifts straight up 62 mm with a Kapton pull tab stuck to its bottom and front face.

quotes: 有没有一种方式可以更方便地换电池？比如能不能用卡扣或者Dual Lock等来实现电池非常方便地拆卸，平时稳定，但是要拆卸的时候也不麻烦。
如果你要设计卡扣的话，PLA的强度是不是足够高？或者能不能通过巧妙的设计，让PLA的强度正好也可以卡住，同时也不会太脆而折断？
approved.history: 2026-11-01: concept sheet concept/concept-sheet.png (top opening, hatch with fixed front tabs and one PLA side snap, bars fixed, pull tab). Shawn asked what the pull tab is (answer: Kapton tape on each battery, 0.05 mm, fits the 0.3 mm play), then 'have a try'. Agent choices after the concept: tongue 1.2 mm (strain 1.3 % at the 1.1 mm release deflection), grip tab behind the box in place of the concept's top knob (the hatch prints top face down), hold-down rib added (without it the battery could rise 8.2 mm to the hatch, the fault the cap cradle was made to remove).
